[[File:Adriana Garroni Oberwolfach 2026.jpg|thumb|Garroni at [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2026]]
'''Adriana Garroni''' (born 1966) is an Italian mathematician specializing in [[mathematical analysis]], including the [[calculus of variations]], [[geometric measure theory]], [[potential theory]], and applications to the mathematical modeling of materials including [[Plasticity (physics)|plasticity]] and [[fracture]]. She is a professor in mathematics at [[Sapienza University of Rome]].

==Education and career==
Garroni was born on 22 March 1966 in Rome,{{r|cv|guido}} and despite having mathematics professor Maria Giovanna Garroni as her mother,{{r|guido|ewm-nl}} she grew up torn between mathematics and the arts.{{r|ewm-nl}}

After earning a [[laurea]] in mathematics in 1991 from Sapienza University of Rome,{{r|cv}} she went to the [[International School for Advanced Studies]] (SISSA) in [[Trieste]] for graduate study in [[functional analysis]] with [[Gianni Dal Maso]], earning an M.Phil. in 1993 and completing her Ph.D. in 1994.{{r|cv|mg}}

She returned to Sapienza University as a researcher in 1995, became an associate professor in 1998, and was named full professor in 2017.{{r|cv}}
